speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can the ungrounded ground another?
premises: She — grasp-less awareness, the subject carried over from v9 — stands unwon in finality (alabdhapariniṣṭhitiḥ) even by her become self (bhūtātmanā, svena).
How then would she go to standing-placehood (pratiṣṭhāspadatām iyāt) for another's being?
Vṛ: ungrounded awareness cannot settle another, as sky-flower yields no scent.
inference: The unself-grounded grounds nothing: v9's inert light cannot found another being.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How does consciousness take on grounding?
premises: Consciousness, apt (ucita) to ground another thing's showing by saying 'this' (idam iti).
And again, by itself (ātmanā), by saying 'I' (aham iti).
Vṛ: the split thing merits showing through this-grasp, then settlement through I-grasp; without rest in I, nothing becomes usable (vyavahārya).
inference: Consciousness fits itself to both poles: 'this' for the other's showing, 'I' for itself.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What orders the inert selves?
premises: By exclusion and inclusion (vyatireketarābhyām — Vṛ: anvayavyatirekābhyām, double concomitance) certainty (niścayaḥ) is called fixed-order, foundation, attainment, completion.
Of the other inert selves (anyajaḍātmanoḥ).
Vṛ: knower settled, the inert stands otherwise; self-and-other certainty runs on presence-and-absence.
inference: Certainty's four offices — order, ground, winning, winding-up — govern inert selves through double concomitance.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What being have inert things?
premises: In self near-unreal (asatkalpāḥ), these inert ones belong to shining alone (prakāśasyaiva).
Shining alone is — of own self, through selves own and other (svaparātmabhiḥ).
Vṛ: without rest in awareness they are near-unreal; shining alone swells, non-separate from its form, in both knower-known heaps — the autonomy-teaching (svātantryavāda) dawns here.
inference: Inert things have only borrowed being: shining alone is, owning both heaps — autonomy's first dawn.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Is there experience without grasp?
premises: No experience (anubhavaḥ) stands apart from distinct-and-indistinct certainty (bhinnābhinnaviniścayam).
None apart from connected shining, grasp-less in its self (vimarśarahitātmanaḥ).

Vṛ: cut from joining-severing autonomy, dull shining yields no relish-experience (saṃrambhātmānubhava); grasp's greatness is housing the world inside as self-one, then outshining it as this, then resting it in full I.
inference: Experience just is grasping certainty; grasp-less shining experiences nothing.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Where does cut-off 'this'-grasping complete?
premises: For this 'this'-grasping cut off (vicchinnavimarśasya), fulfillment (kṛtārthatā) is rest in own form (svasvarūpe viśrāntiḥ).
And that grasping — 'I am this' (so 'ham ity ayam) — is this itself.
Vṛ: the life-principle (jīvitasthānīya) — through it even inert stuff, one with the grasper-self, comes to rest as I; the non-inert are in truth one with the higher knower.
inference: Severed grasping completes in self-rest — 'I am this,' the done-ness that quickens even the inert.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How is the self both bound and free?
premises: The same self (sa eṣa evātmā) twofold: measured (mitaḥ) and unmeasured (aparimitaḥ).
Breath-bound (prāṇādinā niruddhaḥ): atom (aṇuḥ); as supreme self: unbroken (akhaṇḍitaḥ).
Vṛ: the Lord Himself, longing to sport the world-play, shows as breath-selves and contracts into living; uncontracted, He stays full, free awareness-self.
inference: One self, two measures — contracted atom, unbroken whole: play (krīḍā), not split.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What holds both measures?
premises: For both, this (eṣaḥ) is the end-ground (paryantabhūmiḥ) of all object-awarenesses (sarvārthasaṃvidām).
One alone (eka eva) through continuity (anusaṃdhānāt) — before-after joining makes flashing one.
So no other is possible (ato 'nyo nopapadyate).
Vṛ: resting-seat of all being-and-non-being awarenesses; difference cannot hold.
inference: Continuity alone gathers both measures into one end-ground; no second stands.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What shows at the limit?
premises: In I-knowing (ahaṃvidi) whose self is non-separation grasp (avyatirekātma-vimarśātman), limit-dwelling (paryantavartinyām).
Nothing inert beyond shining (bhāsanād adhikaṃ jaḍam) appears (bhāti).

Vṛ: in I-light non-separate from the world — seat of all knowing — the inert has no being past shining's measure; the lone non-inert knower flashes, never fallen from self-seat, outshining and reabsorbing the world-heap.
inference: Seal of the passage: at the limit, shining exhausts the inert; one knower flashes, world outshone and reabsorbed.
